chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii al-Shami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who cultivates another man's land, stipulating for him one-third for the seed and one-third for the oxen.

He said: 'It is not appropriate that he specifies seed and oxen, but he should say to the owner of the land: I will sow in your land and for you from it such and such, half or a third or whatever the condition is, and he does not specify seed and oxen, for it is the speech that prohibits (it).'

key_terms.اَلْبَذْر: Seed; specifically the grain used for sowing.
key_terms.اَلْبَقَر: Oxen/Cattle; specifically the draft animals used for plowing.
key_terms.اَلْكَلاَم: Speech/Verbal specification; referring to the verbal act of specifying inputs which causes the prohibition.
key_terms.اَلْمُزَارَعَة: Sharecropping; a contract where one party provides land and the other provides labor/capital to share the harvest.
key_terms.شَرْط: Condition/Stipulation; the agreed-upon terms of the contract.

ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to structure a sharecropping contract (Muzara'ah) according to Shia hadith to avoid invalidity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition in Muzara'ah targets the uncertainty of inputs (seed and livestock) rather than the output share, a nuance distinguishing it from the stricter Mudarabah contract. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that specifying the means of production introduces gharar, whereas agreeing on a fixed portion of the harvest ensures clarity and fairness in the transaction.
